questions.topic: Manager of record average weekly hours
questions.trigger: During four consecutive representative weeks, a retail pharmacy's manager of record works at the managed pharmacy for 32, 28, 31 and 29 hours. Assume the pattern represents the manager's usual schedule and all other staffing requirements are met. What is the most accurate conclusion about the manager's minimum-hours duty?
questions.legal_decision: An average of 30 hours per week meets the minimum-hours provision.
questions.critical_exception: The standard is an average, not a mandatory identical number every week.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the representative average fell below 30 hours, the minimum-hours duty would not be met.
questions.stem: During four consecutive representative weeks, a retail pharmacy's manager of record works at the managed pharmacy for 32, 28, 31 and 29 hours. Assume the pattern represents the manager's usual schedule and all other staffing requirements are met. What is the most accurate conclusion about the manager's minimum-hours duty?

choices.text: The 28-hour week alone establishes a violation.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision uses an average, not an independent 30-hour minimum for each week.

choices.text: The minimum applies only when the pharmacy is independently owned.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision is not limited to independent ownership.

choices.text: The manager must work 40 hours each week.
choices.why: Incorrect. The specified minimum average is 30 hours.

choices.text: The manager can count hours worked at any other pharmacy toward this requirement.
choices.why: Incorrect. The duty concerns work at the pharmacy under the manager's supervision.

choices.text: The manager meets the average-hours requirement.
choices.why: Correct. The average is 30 hours per week, which meets the stated minimum.

questions.topic: Manager of record documentation of standing orders and technician training
questions.trigger: A retail pharmacy uses two standing orders, including one issued through an external service, and operates an applicable pharmacy technician training program. Which obligations belong to the manager of record? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Maintain copies of all standing orders used; ensure applicable technician training program is Board-approved and current.
questions.critical_exception: An outside issuer does not remove the obligation to retain copies of standing orders used.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the pharmacy has no applicable technician training program, that program-specific duty does not arise.
questions.stem: A retail pharmacy uses two standing orders, including one issued through an external service, and operates an applicable pharmacy technician training program. Which obligations belong to the manager of record? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Retain a copy of the standing order used through the external service.
choices.why: Correct. The manager must ensure copies of all standing orders used are maintained.

choices.text: Treat a training program's prior approval as sufficient even when the program is no longer current.
choices.why: Incorrect. The manager is also responsible for ensuring it is up to date.

choices.text: Ensure the applicable technician training program is Board-approved and up to date.
choices.why: Correct. This is an express manager-of-record responsibility.

choices.text: Transfer both regulatory responsibilities to the external service merely by contract.
choices.why: Incorrect. A contract does not eliminate the manager's assigned duties.

choices.text: Retain only standing orders personally signed by the manager.
choices.why: Incorrect. The duty covers standing orders used, irrespective of who signed them.

questions.topic: Review of duties after temporary pharmacist absence
questions.trigger: A sole pharmacist takes a permitted temporary absence under the pharmacy's written break procedures. Technicians perform only permitted nondiscretionary tasks. On returning, which actions are required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Review duties performed during absence and follow written temporary-absence procedures.
questions.critical_exception: Permission for technical tasks does not waive the pharmacist's review.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If a task required professional judgment, it could not be performed as a nondiscretionary technician task during the break.
questions.stem: A sole pharmacist takes a permitted temporary absence under the pharmacy's written break procedures. Technicians perform only permitted nondiscretionary tasks. On returning, which actions are required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Review only tasks involving Schedule II substances.
choices.why: Incorrect. The review requirement is not limited to Schedule II.

choices.text: Allow technicians to sign off on their own work in place of the required pharmacist review.
choices.why: Incorrect. Technician sign-off does not substitute for the returning pharmacist's responsibility.

choices.text: Review the duties performed by pharmacy personnel during the absence.
choices.why: Correct. The returning pharmacist must review the duties performed during the temporary absence.

choices.text: Follow the pharmacy's written procedures governing temporary absences.
choices.why: Correct. Written policies and procedures are required for these absences.

choices.text: Skip the review whenever a certified technician was present.
choices.why: Incorrect. Certification does not create an exception to the review duty.

critical_error_options.reason: Technician sign-off does not substitute for the returning pharmacist's responsibility.

questions.topic: Individual pharmacist scope of education training and experience
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacist is legally licensed and is asked to independently perform a specialized pharmacy service that is otherwise within the recognized pharmacist scope of practice. The pharmacist has not received the necessary education or training and has no relevant experience. A qualified pharmacist is available to provide the service instead. Which is the best decision?
questions.legal_decision: Do not independently perform a service beyond personal education, training and experience merely because it is within the profession's recognized scope.
questions.critical_exception: Professional scope is necessary but does not substitute for individual competence.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A pharmacist with the requisite education, training and experience may perform a service within recognized scope when all applicable requirements are satisfied.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is legally licensed and is asked to independently perform a specialized pharmacy service that is otherwise within the recognized pharmacist scope of practice. The pharmacist has not received the necessary education or training and has no relevant experience. A qualified pharmacist is available to provide the service instead. Which is the best decision?

choices.text: Perform it because the active license alone establishes competence in every authorized specialty.
choices.why: Incorrect. A general license does not erase the express individual education, training and experience limitation.

choices.text: Ask a qualified pharmacist to provide the service and obtain appropriate preparation before undertaking it independently.
choices.why: Correct. This respects both the recognized scope of practice and the individual pharmacist's competence.

choices.text: Proceed if management signs a document accepting responsibility.
choices.why: Incorrect. Management acceptance does not remove the pharmacist's own professional obligation.

choices.text: Proceed if the patient agrees to waive the pharmacist's training requirement.
choices.why: Incorrect. Patient consent does not override the pharmacist's statutory and regulatory scope limitations.

choices.text: Conclude that no Massachusetts pharmacist may ever provide the service.
choices.why: Incorrect. The facts concern this pharmacist's lack of competence, not a profession-wide prohibition.

critical_error_options.reason: A general license does not erase the express individual education, training and experience limitation.
Management acceptance does not remove the pharmacist's own professional obligation.
Patient consent does not override the pharmacist's statutory and regulatory scope limitations.

questions.topic: Reinstatement after ten-month disciplinary suspension
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration was suspended by the Board for ten months. The suspension period has ended, and the pharmacist applies for registration renewal. Under the rule specific to a suspension of this length, what is required?
questions.legal_decision: Take and pass the MPJE and meet all Board-imposed conditions before renewal following a suspension between six months and two years.
questions.critical_exception: The passage of the suspension period does not itself complete renewal.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For a suspension longer than two years, the separate reinstatement provision expressly identifies NAPLEX as a possible additional condition.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration was suspended by the Board for ten months. The suspension period has ended, and the pharmacist applies for registration renewal. Under the rule specific to a suspension of this length, what is required?

choices.text: Pay a late fee only and resume practice immediately.
choices.why: Incorrect. This is a disciplinary suspension, not an ordinary renewal lapse.

choices.text: Take the NAPLEX only, without satisfying any other Board conditions.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule requires the MPJE and fulfillment of all Board-imposed conditions.

choices.text: Wait until exactly two years have passed before applying.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision does not require waiting two years after a ten-month suspension.

choices.text: Take and pass the MPJE and satisfy all conditions determined by the Board.
choices.why: Correct. For a suspension in this range, both are prerequisites to renewal.

choices.text: Resume practice solely because the suspension term has ended.
choices.why: Incorrect. Expiration of the suspension period does not establish that registration renewal conditions have been fulfilled.

critical_error_options.reason: This is a disciplinary suspension, not an ordinary renewal lapse.
Expiration of the suspension period does not establish that registration renewal conditions have been fulfilled.

questions.topic: Postgraduate courses for continuing education credit
questions.trigger: A registered pharmacist enrolls in a postgraduate pharmacy curriculum, postgraduate pharmacy program or Board-approved postgraduate medical program. Which conditions support continuing education credit for its coursework? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: A satisfactorily completed course in an authorized subject area and qualifying sponsorship may be credited.
questions.critical_exception: Enrollment without satisfactory completion is insufficient.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A course outside the specified subject areas does not qualify merely because it is postgraduate.
questions.stem: A registered pharmacist enrolls in a postgraduate pharmacy curriculum, postgraduate pharmacy program or Board-approved postgraduate medical program. Which conditions support continuing education credit for its coursework? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A course automatically qualifies because the pharmacist paid tuition.
choices.why: Incorrect. Payment does not establish eligibility under the rule.

choices.text: A course unrelated to any qualifying subject solely because it is at graduate level.
choices.why: Incorrect. Graduate status alone does not establish subject-matter eligibility.

choices.text: Sponsorship or cosponsorship of the curriculum or program by a Board-authorized or ACPE-accredited provider.
choices.why: Correct. The curriculum or program must have a qualifying sponsor or cosponsor.

choices.text: Registration for a course that has not yet been completed.
choices.why: Incorrect. Enrollment alone does not demonstrate satisfactory completion.

choices.text: Satisfactory completion of a course in a specified qualifying subject area.
choices.why: Correct. The provision allows credit for satisfactorily completed courses in qualifying areas.

questions.topic: Disciplinary significance of nolo contendere or admission
questions.trigger: A pharmacist enters a plea of nolo contendere in a criminal matter that falls within the Board's disciplinary provision. The pharmacist contends that discipline is impossible because the plea is not a guilty verdict. Which statement is most accurate?
questions.legal_decision: A qualifying nolo contendere plea or admission to sufficient facts may constitute grounds for Board discipline.
questions.critical_exception: A ground for discipline does not itself establish that the license was automatically revoked.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A disposition outside the specified grounds must be assessed under other applicable provisions rather than assumed equivalent.
questions.stem: A pharmacist enters a plea of nolo contendere in a criminal matter that falls within the Board's disciplinary provision. The pharmacist contends that discipline is impossible because the plea is not a guilty verdict. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The Board may consider the plea only if the pharmacist is incarcerated.
choices.why: Incorrect. Incarceration is not a prerequisite stated in this ground.

choices.text: The Board must disregard all criminal dispositions that are not convictions after trial.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision expressly reaches certain other dispositions.

choices.text: The Board may treat a qualifying nolo contendere plea as a ground for discipline.
choices.why: Correct. The disciplinary provision includes such a plea and admission to sufficient facts.

choices.text: Only a guilty verdict after trial can support discipline on criminal grounds.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule includes specified dispositions other than a trial verdict.

choices.text: The plea automatically revokes the registration without any Board action.
choices.why: Incorrect. A disciplinary ground is not equivalent to automatic revocation.

questions.topic: Schedule V antiepileptic and neuropathic pain medications
questions.trigger: A pharmacist receives prescriptions for brivaracetam (Briviact) and pregabalin (Lyrica). What are their federal controlled-substance schedules, assuming the named active ingredients and ordinary finished dosage forms?
questions.legal_decision: Both brivaracetam and pregabalin are Schedule V.
questions.critical_exception: Therapeutic indication does not determine federal scheduling.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An unscheduled prescription-only active ingredient may instead be Massachusetts Schedule VI.
questions.stem: A pharmacist receives prescriptions for brivaracetam (Briviact) and pregabalin (Lyrica). What are their federal controlled-substance schedules, assuming the named active ingredients and ordinary finished dosage forms?

choices.text: Both are Schedule IV.
choices.why: Incorrect. Both are listed in Schedule V.

choices.text: Brivaracetam is Schedule IV; pregabalin is Schedule V.
choices.why: Incorrect. Brivaracetam is Schedule V, not IV.

choices.text: Neither is federally controlled.
choices.why: Incorrect. Both have federal controlled-substance scheduling.

choices.text: Both are Schedule V.
choices.why: Correct. Both active ingredients are listed in federal Schedule V.

choices.text: Brivaracetam is Schedule V; pregabalin is Schedule III.
choices.why: Incorrect. Pregabalin is Schedule V.

questions.topic: Repeat opiate prescription for a minor
questions.trigger: A 16-year-old receives a new outpatient opiate prescription from a practitioner after a previous short course. It is not for treatment of substance use disorder, palliative care or cancer care, and no qualifying exception is documented. Which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: The minor limit applies to subsequent as well as initial prescriptions; required risk and reason discussion with parent or guardian applies.
questions.critical_exception: The adult initial-prescription limitation should not be imported into the rule for minors.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A qualifying documented medical exception may permit a longer supply.
questions.stem: A 16-year-old receives a new outpatient opiate prescription from a practitioner after a previous short course. It is not for treatment of substance use disorder, palliative care or cancer care, and no qualifying exception is documented. Which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The seven-day limit applies to this prescription even though it is not the minor's first.
choices.why: Correct. The provision limits an opiate prescription to a minor at any time, absent an applicable exception.

choices.text: The second prescription may automatically be written for 30 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Prior use alone does not remove the minor-specific limit.

choices.text: The practitioner must discuss the risks associated with opiate use and the reasons the prescription is necessary with the parent or guardian.
choices.why: Correct. The statute requires that discussion for a minor.

choices.text: The seven-day rule applies only to the first opiate prescription in a minor's lifetime.
choices.why: Incorrect. The minor provision is not restricted to an initial prescription.

choices.text: A longer supply is prohibited even when the practitioner satisfies a statutory medical exception.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute permits specified exceptions when their conditions are met.

critical_error_options.reason: Prior use alone does not remove the minor-specific limit.

questions.topic: Revocation of voluntary non-opiate directive
questions.trigger: A competent patient who previously filed a voluntary non-opiate directive tells the treating practitioner orally that the patient wants to revoke it. The practitioner asks whether a new written form is always required to revoke the directive. Which is correct?
questions.legal_decision: The patient may revoke the directive orally or in writing for any reason.
questions.critical_exception: Revocation does not obligate a practitioner to prescribe an opiate.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the patient does not revoke the directive, the applicable restrictions remain.
questions.stem: A competent patient who previously filed a voluntary non-opiate directive tells the treating practitioner orally that the patient wants to revoke it. The practitioner asks whether a new written form is always required to revoke the directive. Which is correct?

choices.text: Revocation automatically entitles the patient to an opiate prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. Removing the directive does not override clinical judgment or other prescribing law.

choices.text: Only the practitioner who originally filed the directive may approve revocation.
choices.why: Incorrect. The patient may revoke it; the statute does not make revocation contingent on that practitioner's approval.

choices.text: The directive may be revoked orally or in writing.
choices.why: Correct. The statute permits revocation by either means for any reason.

choices.text: Revocation is permitted only in a medical emergency.
choices.why: Incorrect. Revocation is permitted for any reason.

choices.text: Revocation must be notarized.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute does not impose that condition.

questions.topic: Nuclear pharmacy oral prescription record
questions.trigger: An authorized practitioner communicates a lawful oral prescription for a radiopharmaceutical to a nuclear pharmacist. Which actions or record elements are required under the nuclear pharmacy prescription provision? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Reduce the oral prescription to writing immediately and record the required prescription details, including dose and serial number.
questions.critical_exception: The nuclear prescription record is a specific statutory requirement.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An otherwise valid written order does not require reduction from oral form, although the applicable record duties remain.
questions.stem: An authorized practitioner communicates a lawful oral prescription for a radiopharmaceutical to a nuclear pharmacist. Which actions or record elements are required under the nuclear pharmacy prescription provision? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Immediately reduce the oral prescription to writing.
choices.why: Correct. The statute expressly requires immediate reduction to writing.

choices.text: Omit the record whenever the order is from a familiar practitioner.
choices.why: Incorrect. Familiarity with the prescriber does not eliminate the record requirement.

choices.text: Include the prescription serial number.
choices.why: Correct. The statute includes a serial number among the record elements.

choices.text: Include the prescribed dose in the required record.
choices.why: Correct. The dose is a required element of the nuclear prescription.

choices.text: Wait until the end of the month to reduce the order to writing.
choices.why: Incorrect. Delayed monthly transcription does not satisfy the immediate requirement.

questions.topic: Multiple Schedule II prescriptions are discretionary
questions.trigger: A patient requests that a physician issue several Schedule II prescriptions at one visit for a total of 90 days. The physician believes that more frequent visits are clinically appropriate. Assuming all applicable federal and state rules are considered, what does the federal multiple-prescription rule require?
questions.legal_decision: It permits qualifying multiple prescriptions but neither mandates nor encourages a 90-day arrangement.
questions.critical_exception: Clinical judgment controls whether to issue multiple prescriptions or schedule more frequent visits.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the practitioner chooses multiple prescriptions, all conditions and state-law requirements must be satisfied.
questions.stem: A patient requests that a physician issue several Schedule II prescriptions at one visit for a total of 90 days. The physician believes that more frequent visits are clinically appropriate. Assuming all applicable federal and state rules are considered, what does the federal multiple-prescription rule require?

choices.text: The physician must issue a single Schedule II prescription with two refills.
choices.why: Incorrect. Schedule II prescriptions cannot be refilled.

choices.text: The regulation requires every Schedule II patient to return every 30 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. The federal rule does not establish a universal visit interval.

choices.text: The physician must issue prescriptions totaling 90 days whenever the patient requests them.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation expressly does not mandate such issuance.

choices.text: A federal 90-day authorization makes any conflicting state limit inapplicable.
choices.why: Incorrect. Compliance with applicable state law is an express condition.

choices.text: The physician may decide that more frequent visits are appropriate and decline the requested multiple-prescription arrangement.
choices.why: Correct. The rule is permissive and leaves visit frequency to professional judgment.

questions.topic: Community CDTM therapy extension beyond ordinary periods
questions.trigger: A qualified Massachusetts community pharmacist practicing under a valid collaborative drug therapy management agreement has already extended a patient's existing therapy for two 30-day periods. The supervising physician specifically authorizes an additional extension in the patient's referral, and the agreement expressly provides for that authorization. All other requirements are satisfied. Which conclusion is most accurate?
questions.legal_decision: An otherwise specifically authorized extension may be permitted when both the referral and CDTM agreement support it.
questions.critical_exception: The ordinary two-period limit is subject to the express authorization provision.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the referral or agreement does not support the additional extension, the ordinary limit controls.
questions.stem: A qualified Massachusetts community pharmacist practicing under a valid collaborative drug therapy management agreement has already extended a patient's existing therapy for two 30-day periods. The supervising physician specifically authorizes an additional extension in the patient's referral, and the agreement expressly provides for that authorization. All other requirements are satisfied. Which conclusion is most accurate?

choices.text: A third extension is never permitted regardless of the referral and agreement.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision expressly recognizes a specific authorization pathway.

choices.text: The agreement alone authorizes every additional extension even without the specified referral authorization.
choices.why: Incorrect. The patient's referral is also necessary for this exception.

choices.text: The additional extension may be permitted under the specific referral and agreement authorization.
choices.why: Correct. The rule provides an exception to the ordinary limit when otherwise specifically authorized in the referral and provided for in the agreement.

choices.text: The referral alone always supersedes a conflicting collaborative agreement.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule requires the arrangement to be provided for in the agreement as well.

choices.text: The pharmacist may extend indefinitely without referral authorization after two extensions.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception requires specific physician authorization and agreement coverage.

critical_error_options.reason: The exception requires specific physician authorization and agreement coverage.

questions.topic: Vaccines drawn up for future use under Massachusetts policy
questions.trigger: For a scheduled clinic, pharmacy personnel plan to draw vaccine doses into syringes more than one hour before anticipated administration. Under the Massachusetts Board vaccine administration policy, what is the appropriate regulatory approach?
questions.legal_decision: Drawing vaccines for future use beyond one hour is treated as sterile compounding under USP <797>.
questions.critical_exception: The Board's vaccine-specific future-use provision must be considered rather than relying on the general immediate-use timing rule alone.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Manufacturer-supplied prefilled syringes are not the same as pharmacy personnel drawing doses for future use.
questions.stem: For a scheduled clinic, pharmacy personnel plan to draw vaccine doses into syringes more than one hour before anticipated administration. Under the Massachusetts Board vaccine administration policy, what is the appropriate regulatory approach?

choices.text: Treat the doses as outside sterile compounding because a clinic is scheduled.
choices.why: Incorrect. A scheduled clinic does not create this exemption.

choices.text: Consider the doses manufacturer-prefilled because the pharmacy filled them in advance.
choices.why: Incorrect. Pharmacy preparation is not manufacturer prefilling.

choices.text: Treat the planned preparation as sterile compounding subject to USP <797>.
choices.why: Correct. The Board policy addresses doses drawn for future use more than one hour in advance.

choices.text: Use only the general USP immediate-use timing rule and disregard the vaccine-specific policy.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Massachusetts policy specifically addresses advance preparation of vaccines.

choices.text: Avoid the applicable sterile compounding requirements by assigning the preparation to a technician.
choices.why: Incorrect. The person performing the task does not remove the preparation's regulatory classification.

questions.citation: Massachusetts Board Policy 2023-02, Vaccine Administration, VIII(B); USP <797>

critical_error_options.reason: The person performing the task does not remove the preparation's regulatory classification.

questions.topic: Alternative method for offer to counsel when ordinary communication unavailable
questions.trigger: A patient cannot use the pharmacy's usual face-to-face or telephone communication methods because of individual communication needs. The pharmacist can use an effective, appropriate alternative method to communicate privately with the patient. What is the best approach to the required offer to counsel?
questions.legal_decision: Make the offer through an appropriate alternative method when the patient's needs or availability require it.
questions.critical_exception: Alternative communication does not dispense with the actual offer or counseling when accepted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: When face-to-face or telephone communication meets the patient's needs, the ordinary methods apply.
questions.stem: A patient cannot use the pharmacy's usual face-to-face or telephone communication methods because of individual communication needs. The pharmacist can use an effective, appropriate alternative method to communicate privately with the patient. What is the best approach to the required offer to counsel?

choices.text: Use the appropriate alternative communication method to make the offer and provide counseling if accepted.
choices.why: Correct. The statute allows another method when the patient's needs or availability require it.

choices.text: Postpone the offer until the patient can communicate by telephone, regardless of other suitable methods.
choices.why: Incorrect. An appropriate alternative may be used when the patient's needs require it.

choices.text: Supply written material alone without making an offer.
choices.why: Incorrect. Written information is not a substitute for the required offer.

choices.text: Ask an unqualified employee to independently provide the professional counseling.
choices.why: Incorrect. The alternative method does not expand personnel scope of practice.

choices.text: Treat the patient as having refused because telephone communication is not possible.
choices.why: Incorrect. Inability to use one method is not a refusal.

critical_error_options.reason: Inability to use one method is not a refusal.

questions.topic: Counseling signs at multiple dispensing areas
questions.trigger: A retail pharmacy has two separate areas at which prescriptions are dispensed. It is redesigning its patient counseling notices. Which measures satisfy the specific location and minimum-size requirements for counseling signs? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Post required signage adjacent to each dispensing area, at least 11 by 14 inches with letters at least one-half inch high.
questions.critical_exception: A compliant sign in one separate dispensing area does not satisfy the adjacent-to-each requirement for the other.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A single dispensing area requires signage adjacent to that area.
questions.stem: A retail pharmacy has two separate areas at which prescriptions are dispensed. It is redesigning its patient counseling notices. Which measures satisfy the specific location and minimum-size requirements for counseling signs? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Use letters at least one-half inch high.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation establishes this minimum lettering height.

choices.text: Use smaller lettering because the pharmacy provides counseling on request.
choices.why: Incorrect. Providing counseling does not waive the specified sign dimensions.

choices.text: Use signs at least 11 inches high by 14 inches wide.
choices.why: Correct. That is the stated minimum sign size.

choices.text: Place the required notice adjacent to each dispensing area.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation specifies placement adjacent to each dispensing area.

choices.text: Place one sign only in the employee break room.
choices.why: Incorrect. That does not satisfy the required public-facing location.

questions.topic: HIPAA agreed restriction during emergency treatment
questions.trigger: A covered pharmacy previously agreed to a patient's restriction on disclosure of certain protected health information for treatment. The patient later needs emergency treatment, and the restricted information is necessary to provide that treatment. Which actions are consistent with HIPAA? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Disclose necessary restricted information for emergency treatment and request that the receiving provider not further use or disclose it except to provide emergency treatment.
questions.critical_exception: The emergency exception concerns information needed for emergency treatment, not ordinary convenience.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Without the emergency-treatment necessity or another applicable exception, the agreed restriction must be honored.
questions.stem: A covered pharmacy previously agreed to a patient's restriction on disclosure of certain protected health information for treatment. The patient later needs emergency treatment, and the restricted information is necessary to provide that treatment. Which actions are consistent with HIPAA? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Request that the receiving provider not further use or disclose the restricted information except to provide emergency treatment.
choices.why: Correct. When disclosing restricted information under this exception, the covered entity must request that the recipient limit further use or disclosure to emergency treatment.

choices.text: Disclose the entire restricted record to unrelated recipients because the patient is in an emergency.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception is tied to the emergency treatment need.

choices.text: Conclude that HIPAA forbids disclosure of information needed for emergency treatment solely because the restriction was agreed to.
choices.why: Incorrect. The emergency exception permits disclosure of restricted information needed for emergency treatment.

choices.text: Treat the restriction as permanently canceled by the emergency disclosure.
choices.why: Incorrect. An emergency disclosure does not automatically terminate the agreed restriction.

choices.text: Disclose the restricted information needed for emergency treatment to the treating provider.
choices.why: Correct. HIPAA permits this use or disclosure when the information is needed for emergency treatment.

critical_error_options.reason: The exception is tied to the emergency treatment need.

questions.topic: Schedule II narcotic fax for direct parenteral infusion
questions.trigger: A practitioner issues a signed Schedule II narcotic prescription for compounding for direct administration to a patient by parenteral infusion. It is faxed to the pharmacy. Assume a valid Massachusetts electronic-prescribing exception and all other prescription and compounding requirements are met. Under federal law, how may the pharmacist treat the fax?
questions.legal_decision: The fax may serve as the original written prescription for this specified parenteral infusion exception.
questions.critical_exception: The exception does not extend to all outpatient Schedule II prescriptions or every injectable product.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the prescription is not within an applicable fax-as-original exception, the ordinary original-prescription requirement applies.
questions.stem: A practitioner issues a signed Schedule II narcotic prescription for compounding for direct administration to a patient by parenteral infusion. It is faxed to the pharmacy. Assume a valid Massachusetts electronic-prescribing exception and all other prescription and compounding requirements are met. Under federal law, how may the pharmacist treat the fax?

choices.text: Accept the fax as the original written prescription under the specific infusion-compounding exception.
choices.why: Correct. Federal law expressly permits this for a Schedule II narcotic compounded for direct parenteral infusion.

choices.text: Require the paper original in every case, including the specified exception.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule recognizes a fax-as-original exception on these facts.

choices.text: Convert the fax into a refillable Schedule II order.
choices.why: Incorrect. Fax acceptance does not permit Schedule II refills.

choices.text: Use the fax exception to disregard applicable Massachusetts electronic-prescribing requirements.
choices.why: Incorrect. The federal exception does not displace state requirements.

choices.text: Accept any outpatient Schedule II fax as the original whenever the drug is injectable.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception is specific to the described compounding and administration circumstances.

critical_error_options.reason: The exception is specific to the described compounding and administration circumstances.

questions.topic: Pharmacist knowledge of voluntary non-opiate directive
questions.trigger: An outpatient pharmacist receives an otherwise valid electronic opiate prescription. The pharmacist has no information that the prescriber acted against a voluntary non-opiate directive and no unresolved red flags. How does Massachusetts's non-opiate directive statute address the pharmacist in these circumstances?
questions.legal_decision: The statute protects the pharmacist from liability for dispensing a valid prescription except where the pharmacist has knowledge it was issued in violation of the directive.
questions.critical_exception: The protection does not excuse knowing violation or displace other dispensing obligations.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the pharmacist knows the order was issued against an unrevoked applicable directive, the protection does not apply.
questions.stem: An outpatient pharmacist receives an otherwise valid electronic opiate prescription. The pharmacist has no information that the prescriber acted against a voluntary non-opiate directive and no unresolved red flags. How does Massachusetts's non-opiate directive statute address the pharmacist in these circumstances?

choices.text: The pharmacist is protected even when knowingly dispensing a prescription issued in violation of the directive.
